passages.title: Benefits Summary & Eligibility
passages.text:
Employees of the Toronto office are covered by the RSE Canada Group Plan, which provides health, dental and other group benefits for Canadian employees. This summary does not describe the plan in detail. Plan details, claims and eligibility questions for the RSE Canada Group Plan go to HR.
The US plan descriptions in §2 do not apply to Toronto employees, even where the plans have similar names. Toronto employees enrol in the RSE Canada Group Plan through HR when they join, and HR provides the plan booklet and claim forms.

passages.title: Benefits Summary & Eligibility
passages.text:
Feature | Dental
Preventive care | Cleanings and check-ups covered in network
Basic and major care | Fillings, crowns and other treatment shared with the plan
You can join the dental plan even if you waive medical coverage, and you can choose a different coverage level for dental than for medical. Details of the dental network are in the plan documents.

passages.title: Benefits Summary & Eligibility
passages.text:
For anything this summary doesn't answer, including claims, plan details and costs, the RSE Canada Group Plan, or your own coverage, contact the HR Service Desk at hr@ridgeline.example or through HR Portal > Ask HR.
This document is a summary. Where it differs from the plan documents, the plan documents apply. HR can explain how the plans work but cannot advise you which plan is best for your personal circumstances.

passages.title: Benefits Summary & Eligibility
passages.text:
Benefits eligibility depends on your Employment Type. Full-time employees are eligible for all US plans in §2. Part-time employees are eligible for medical, dental, vision and the 401(k); Ridgeline's employer contribution to medical premiums is pro-rated by scheduled hours. Interns are eligible for the 401(k) only. Contractors are not eligible for Ridgeline benefits. Employees of the Toronto office are covered by the RSE Canada Group Plan instead of the US plans (§5).
Your eligibility is based on the Employment Type on your HR record. If your Employment Type changes, for example from part-time to full-time, your eligibility changes from the date of the change, and you can update your elections within the qualifying life event window (§3.4).

passages.title: Benefits Summary & Eligibility
passages.text:
For medical, dental and vision you choose one coverage level: employee only, employee plus spouse, employee plus children, or family.
You can choose a different coverage level for each plan, for example family medical coverage and employee-only vision. Your coverage level stays the same for the plan year unless you have a qualifying life event (§3.4).

passages.title: Work Location, Travel & Cross-Border Work Guidelines
passages.text:
Your work location is the work region and country on your HR record, for example Colorado, US or Ontario, Canada. Your work location decides which rules apply when you work from somewhere else, whether that is business travel (§2) or temporary remote work (RSE-RW-01 §6).
For most employees the work location is the state or province of their home office. Remote-approved employees may have a different work region, which is recorded when their arrangement is approved. Keep your work location up to date: it affects payroll, benefits and which holiday calendar applies.

passages.title: Travel & Expense Reimbursement
passages.text: Attach an itemised receipt for every item of $25 or more. A card statement is not a receipt. Photograph paper receipts and attach them to your claim in the HR Portal. If a receipt is lost, explain on the claim; your manager decides whether to approve it.
